setupSteps.title: Install Git
setupSteps.verifierLabel: Git responds with a version number

setupSteps.title: Install Node LTS
setupSteps.verifierLabel: Node responds with a version number

steps.title: Open Terminal
steps.body: Keep it open beside Iris.

steps.title: Check Git and Node
steps.body: chatmany's deploy tool needs Node 22 or newer.
steps.verifierLabel: Git and Node respond with version numbers

hints: If node prints a version below v22, install the current LTS from the setup steps — the deploy tool refuses to run on older Node.
If either line says "command not found", install it from the setup steps, then open a new terminal window.

steps.title: Copy chatmany to this Mac
steps.command:
cd ~
if [ ! -d chatmany/.git ]; then
git clone https://github.com/Blueturboguy07/chatmany.git
fi
cd chatmany
git checkout aa0888ffe73e880bb90dbc588665981d9a53d205
steps.verifierLabel: You are inside the chatmany folder

hints: If Git says the destination path 'chatmany' already exists, you cloned it on an earlier attempt — carry on.

steps.title: Install the deploy tool
steps.body: A few hundred small packages, including wrangler — Cloudflare's deploy tool.

steps.title: Sign in to Cloudflare
steps.body: A browser opens — sign in to your free Cloudflare account and click Allow.
steps.verifierLabel: The terminal prints Successfully logged in

expect.prompt: In the terminal, has wrangler login finished — is there a line reading "Successfully logged in.", rather than a timeout error?

hints: No Cloudflare account yet? Create a free one at dash.cloudflare.com first, then run the command again.
If the login times out, run the command again and click Allow within five minutes.

steps.title: Create the database
steps.body: Copy the database_id it prints — the next step needs it.

steps.title: Put the database id in the config
steps.body: In wrangler.toml, replace REPLACE-WITH-THE-ID-FROM-wrangler-d1-create with your database_id.

steps.title: Set up the database tables
steps.verifierLabel: Three migrations show a check mark

steps.title: Put chatmany online
steps.body: The printed workers.dev address is MY ADDRESS from here on — write it down.

expect.prompt: In the terminal, has wrangler deploy finished with a https://….workers.dev address and a Current Version ID line, with no error after them?

hints: If it says it could not register "chatmany" as your workers.dev subdomain, your account has no subdomain yet and that name is taken: open the Cloudflare dashboard link in the error, register any free subdomain name there, then run the deploy again.
The new address can show a security error for the first minute while its certificate is issued — wait a minute and reload instead of debugging.

steps.title: Tell the config its own address
steps.body: In wrangler.toml, set REDIRECT_URI to MY ADDRESS + /auth/callback.

steps.title: Deploy again
steps.body: Same command — it now ships the config with your address in it.

steps.title: Set your owner password
steps.body: Invent a long random password, paste it when asked, and keep a copy — it is your only login.
steps.verifierLabel: wrangler reports the secret was uploaded

hints: Any long random string works. `openssl rand -hex 32` in a second terminal prints a good one.

steps.title: Create your Meta app
steps.body: On developers.facebook.com: My Apps, Create app, use case Manage messaging & content on Instagram.
steps.verifierLabel: The new app's dashboard is open

steps.title: Copy the Instagram app ID and secret
steps.body: Use cases, Customize, API setup with Instagram login. Add all required permissions, then copy both.
steps.verifierLabel: Instagram app ID and secret are in your notes

hints: Wrong-pair trap: App settings → Basic also shows an App ID and secret. That pair installs fine and then fails at the very last step. Use ONLY the pair labelled Instagram app ID / Instagram app secret on the API setup page.
The "Add all required permissions" click can silently not register — re-click until the section shows a green check.

steps.title: Register your address with Meta
steps.body: On the same page: Set up Instagram business login. Enter MY ADDRESS + /auth/callback and save.

hints: The redirect URL lives in TWO places: the Set up dialog and the Business login settings button below it. After saving the first, open Business login settings and confirm the same URL is listed there.
While in Business login settings, put MY ADDRESS + /data-deletion in the data deletion field.

steps.title: Fill in the app's public pages
steps.body: App settings, Basic: set privacy, terms and data deletion to MY ADDRESS + those three pages.

hints: The three URLs, exactly: MY ADDRESS/privacy, MY ADDRESS/terms, MY ADDRESS/data-deletion — chatmany serves all three pages itself.
Pick any category (Messaging fits). These fields unlock the Publish button — it stays grey until they are saved.

steps.title: Publish the app
steps.body: Sidebar, Publish, then the Publish button. The sidebar badge must say Published.

hints: This step is silent but load-bearing: an unpublished app returns empty comment and message lists with no error at all — everything looks fine and nothing works.

steps.title: Add the Instagram Tester role
steps.body: App roles, Roles, Add People, pick Instagram Tester, type your Instagram username, Add.
steps.verifierLabel: Your username is listed as Instagram Tester

hints: Do not skip this. Without it every Instagram call fails with "Unsupported request - method type: get" — an error that never mentions roles.
Older write-ups place this on the Customize page and call the failure Insufficient Developer Role; both moved. The role now lives under App roles → Roles.

steps.title: Accept the tester invite
steps.body: On instagram.com in a computer browser: Settings, Apps and websites, Tester Invites, Accept.

hints: Desktop browser only — the Instagram phone app has no Tester Invites screen anywhere, so this cannot be done from a phone.
If chatmany later fails with "Unsupported request - method type: get", this invite (or the role step before it) was skipped — the error is misleading and this is the fix.

steps.title: Give chatmany the Meta credentials
steps.body: Run each line, pasting the Instagram app ID for the first and the secret for the second.
steps.command:
npx wrangler secret put APP_ID
npx wrangler secret put APP_SECRET

hints: These are the two values from the API setup with Instagram login page — the Instagram pair, not the Basic-settings pair.

steps.title: Connect your Instagram account
steps.body: Open MY ADDRESS + /auth/authorize, then click Allow on Instagram's permission screen.

hints: An "Invalid state (possible CSRF)" page means the browser loaded the start page twice — just go to /auth/authorize again and Allow; it works on the retry.
You are typing your password on instagram.com, never into chatmany — it only receives a token afterwards.

steps.title: Open your dashboard
steps.body: Open MY ADDRESS, sign in with your owner password, and build your first automation.
steps.verifierLabel: The dashboard shows your Instagram handle

hints: To test a funnel you need a SECOND Instagram account — any personal one works. Your own account cannot trigger its own campaign, because chatmany would have to DM itself.
Comments are checked about every 90 seconds, so give a test comment a couple of minutes before concluding something is wrong.
